title: the model of taking electronic medical records as the core for information construction in hospitals
display_name: The model of “taking electronic medical records as the core for information construction in hospitals”
abstract: the development of hospital information has been carried out for nearly 50 years, and originally started as the hospital information system (his).1 so far his is the most widely and deeply used management system for hospitals in china.2 "general function standard for hospital information system" issued by china's ministry of health in 2002 defined that "the hospital information system refers to using of computer hardware and software technology, network communications technology, and other modern technology to comprehensively manage personnel, logistics, and finance in various departments in hospital. gather, store, treat, extract, transport, aggregate, and process data in various stages of the medical activities, so that provide comprehensive and automatic information management and service to the hospital." as a result, comprehensive management based on personnel, logistics, finance, and hospital overall operation management are always the focus of hospital information construction.3,4 in the past 10 years, to comply with the development of health reforms in china, hospitals have stronger demand for clinical information, laboratory information system (lis), picture archiving and communication system (pacs), and nurse information system (nis), which emerged one by one.5 they indicate that the information construction in china has developed in depth, satisfying hospitals' professional demands gradually. it also reflects the demand for hospitals to take responsibility, complete business, pursue service target and objectives, which in hospitals is to provide clinical health service to the patients. one of the roots of information construction is the sharing of the information and concerned historical reasons. subsequent systems have to be grafted into his, and hence the core of the hospital information framework was formed. since 2009, the department of health has issued regulations as "basic architecture and data standards for electronic medical record (pilot)" and "electronic medical record system function standard (pilot)", to make the electronic medical record of the hospital information construction as the new theme and focus. hence, the original framework cannot fit into the hospital information construction development any more. characteristics and innovation in chinese hospital information construction electronic medical records (emrs) include a wide-range of information: patients, diseases, treatment processes, hospitals, medical stuff, nation policy, and other information that directly record and reflect the functions of hospitals, medical care work, and medical care quality.6,7 with all the clinical information systems like ris, lis, nis, anesthesia system, pass, remote medical, and other systems that have been used widely in hospitals, large volume of medical information that relates to patients must be integrated to emr, but they do not have close connections with his. as a result, at the core of emr, the hospital information construction is put forward naturally, and has become the new stage for the hospital information construction. the concept of emr in 1997, computer-based patient record institute (cpri) has stated the definition for emr: "the content of emr contains all paper based information, but it is not only the transport of paper based information into computer based information, but also the transfer of the word, image, and voice from paper based medical records into data format that can be scanned, stored, processed and inquired by the computer.8 it contains not only the static medical record information but also the comprehensive processing of the text, image, and voice by using multi-media information technology". electronic health record system (ehr-s, also emr) refers to a system of recording, retrieving, and processing electronic medical information (reference to "iso/ts 18308, cen 13606"). the institute of medicine (iom) indicated advances in 2003 that: ehr-s collect individual's electronic health information (include personal health condition and medical services),9 only an authorized user can get the relevant individual information or group information to improve health service quality (safety and efficiency) and efficiency of the health service departments. if we treat electronic health records as health information set, then ehr is the systems that form, operate, and utilize the information set.10 it must have the following functions: can process various health care data (include image, number, text etc.); can implement medical data access, support medical business, support clinical decision, manage health data, and so on; can integrate many different systems together (including lis, pacs, nis, and cdss); can share information by all the authorized users. electronic health system is highly complicated, and is the core of all the information systems in the hospital. essence of emr in the development of emr, at first, people placed electronic scanning documents, manual entry word text or form type medical records in a computer, called emr.11,12 but in essence, it just transplanted paper medium medical records into an electronic carrier; the computer does not understand the information. therefore, the essence of emr is that it can be identified, understood and processed by computers. a computer can partly recognize and understand the current semi-structured emr.13 trend of emr development in china and aboard emr is the focus of medical health information construction all around the world.14 for example, in the statement of national condition and presidential election of the former us president george w. bush instructed to call off all the paper based medical records, and the federal government setup a 125 million dollars fund to implement emr. obama said in the congress speech in february 2009, that the health profile for every american citizen will be set up in the future 5 years, and 17 billion dollars will be put to reward and utilize emr. in the last 20 years, all developed countries took various actions to put forward emr research and make emr universal. china has started research on emr development since the 1990s; in 2005 the health department drew up "e-health" plan in "eleventh five-year", and put the emr as the key construction in the plan. since 2009 all policy regulations were issued by the health department, emr has become the focus of hospital information construction. the health department just issued "electronic medical record system functional level of application, classification, and evaluation methods and standards (pilot)", and this will further standardize the emr system in china, clarify functions needed to implement for every development stage, and guided the hospital to develop emr systems scientifically. "taking emr as the core for hospital information construction" project xinhua hospital affiliated to the shanghai jiao tong university school of medicine is a general 3 a hospital integrated with medical, teaching, research, disease prevention, health care, and rehabilitation. with 10 years of effort, xinhua has transformed from stage one which was oriented in "personnel, finance, cargo" to stage two which was oriented to clinical information management.15 to fulfill the information construction blueprint, the hospital will research and develop the new emr, and locate the target on "take the patient as the core, take the business personnel as the core, support health care decisions, and improve health care quality". new emr framework model with reference to advanced foreign experience, with as-is condition in china and xinhua hospital, as the core of clinical data repository (cdr) and controlled medical vocabulary (cmv), we establish the whole architecture of an emr system. xinhua has established a medical data center that can store and manage standardized information expression for a long time and supported by medical terminology. medical knowledge base is the root and principle to understand, derive and apply medical data correctly. the triple is the core of emr. the integrated platform is the basic integrated setting for every information system in hospitals (like his, lis, pacs etc.), and it satisfies integration of work-flow between systems and data integration, and is located on the bottom layer of an emr. on the other hand, the doctor workstation and nurse workstation is the presentation layer. clinical decision support system (cdss), computerized physician order entry (cpoe), and pharmacy information system (pis) are the periphery of emr system. they are the functions implemented by emr and have the potential to continuously deepen and expand.16 clinical document application is the technical method to implement emrs; for the basic framework refer to figure 1.figure 1.: emr major framework.emr integrated view in the integrated view, various emr data relationships will be clear at one glance. medical personnel can not only observe the various types of indicators to capture the overall progression of the disease and directly access the changing circumstances of the disease, the patient diagnosis, and treatment plans developed by the implementation of its clinical effects, but also can easily read the historical data of the patient's medical records, which provide a wealth of reference information for the next stage of diagnosis and treatment. the last can be directly based on the various types of medical data in the medical view, to visualize the form of most of the day-to-day work, including written records showing the doctor's advice, inspection, testing, prescription, treatment, surgery, and care. the patient browsing sign interface, can provide quick and precise information on life sign, medical order, inspection, and checkups to doctors. establish new clinical, full close loop management traditional cope is the sub-system of his, and its main function is to manage the expenses and logistics (medicine), medical order execution, and effectiveness but it has no monitoring ability. new ehr brings cope into the her framework, and it has become the medical plan from diagnosis to implementation of the close-loop management (medical order - nurse check - pharmacy row medicine), it is dynamically displayed on the medical records. this is the key element in the her grading evaluation standard. xinhua hospital's medical order whole process management has message task management center, task remind, and report reminder functions, it lets the doctor know the medical processing time and the exceptions, and it controls all the links. integration platform construction as one patient's medical record information will be distributed in different information systems in a hospital, medical information integration is a problem that must be solved through the emr system.17 xinhua hospital made the emr system the information gathering center, and formed the emr integration scope and framework with all the information sources and information destinations. all treatment information will finally be integrated into the emr system. the key technology of emr integration is how to integrate the existing heterogeneous systems (his, lis, pacs system developed by different vendors) into the emr system. xinhua hospital has imported an advanced foreign integration platform, uses the international accepted standard interface, like hl7, and integrates the medical information into the emr system seamlessly in the whole hospital.18 clinical decision support system and clinical pathway wyatt and spiegel halter have very precise definition for clinical decision support system (cdss): according to two or more than two patients' data, it generates corresponding disease case suggested knowledge system. this definition clarifies that cdss needs to contain three major elements: medical knowledge, patient data, and detailed treatment suggestion. clinical doctors need to make decisions on the patients' treatment procedure: what inspection needs to be taken? what is the disease diagnosis? which medicine should be given? is surgery required? and what is the treatment effect. all these clinical decisions must be based on patient data, medical knowledge, and records of medical order, medical record analysis, and diagnosis into the emr system. as a result, emr system has necessary internal connections with cdss.19,20 the cdss function in emr system can standardize the medical personnel health care behavior, improve medical quality; modify wrong medical behavior in time, prevent medical errors and accidents; move the quality and safety from the terminal link to the intermediate link. 'clinical pathway' and 'clinical guidance', 'remind and warn', 'medical expert system' all belong to cdss. xinhua hospital cdss function has the rational medicine, antibiotic management, medical process quality control and clinical pathway, they provide services to the doctor in the following ways: (1) according to clinical work-flow, gather information from various information system, then display to doctors. (2) provide online medical knowledge base to read and reference. (3) provide a part of real-time decision support to the clinical activities. (4) provide warnings and reminders against part of the medical problem and wrong decisions. as clinical pathway (cp) will design the best medical care plan, implementation approach and standardize the treatment procedure according to different disease and patient condition, it will shorten the average days in hospital, thus reducing the hospitalization expense. health department issued "clinical pathway management pilot plan" in 2009, making cp one of the focus of health information construction. currently most cp management is based on paper, linear, by hand mode. xinhua hospital has developed a multi-diseases electronic cp, and embedded them into the emr system, making cp, cpoe, and emr integrated together. in this way, you can choose the corresponding cp according to patient emr information; generate medical orders automatically; import medical orders into emr automatically, and generate corresponding records in the emr system. structured emr based on controlled medical terminology xinhua hospital's new emrs system has established controlled medical vocabulary (cmv). as all the terms referring to medical theory, have only term identifiers, 'enter' patient data or clinical data into structured emrs under cmv will change into formatted data that can be recognized by emr, and then it will have various 'intelligence' like cp, cdss etc. cmv also can support multi-organization data sharing. currently internationally used terminology systems include icd-10, snomed-ct, loinc, and so on. as standard terminology construction will not cover all the fields, cmv has a part of 'self-set' medical terminology, and it takes technology to make them compatible to standard controlled vocabulary. establish medical knowledge base medical knowledge base is the core of emr, and it is the basis of quality management of emr system. when we 'enter' a patient's symptom, sign, inspection result, and so on, it is actually calling the 'fact' and 'rules' in the knowledge base. by knowledge reasoning, it derives the disease diagnosis and treatment plan. xinhua hospital emr knowledge base is still in the setup stage; it will refer to quality management requirement in this stage, and it will be built up by subject matter experts and it personnel gradually. it will help physicians access the knowledge base in time by emr system to get relevant medical knowledge to make the right medical decision. new emr support the close-loop management for the whole patient medical flow throughout the medical procedure, there are five links: (1) observation: include interrogation, body check, sign, symptom, and medical history information. (2) diagnosis: based on the above information the patient's major problem can be found diagnosis and differential diagnosis. (3) planning: infer the patient's medical order and medical treatment program. (4) implementation: implement and test medical order; (5) assessment: evaluate patient's medical link (like one day, one course of treatment), and recorded it in the emr system; if the treatment is effective, then keep the former plan on; if the treatment is not, then enter into the next loop (figure 2).figure 2.: new emrs support the close-loop management for a whole medical flow.paper based medical records and present emrs can only be used in the link. the new emr system uses the patient's treatment cycle as the time axis, and every event in the treatment procedure as the trigger condition. it uses the intelligence as the display, and makes it reflect into the emr system integrate so that the whole medical order process status can be monitored, and this helps provide intelligent decision support. powerful health care workstation doctor and nurse workstation is the representative of the work-flow integration and data integration, enabling emrs entry, storage, processing, display, and application, implementation of digital signature, trace retention and template production, provide consistent emr integrated views and data integrated browse views to improve the ease of use. medical care workstation should contain the following modules: medical records integrated view; computerized medical order system; data browsing view; clinical path system; standardized structured clinical document editing system; various knowledge base system; cdss; mobile medical care workstation system. new emr construction implementation target of new emr design phase i construction will include: emr basic framework and basic business, based on the controlled terminology structured entering format, integration platform, medical order whole process close-loop management (message task management center, like task reminder, report reminder, and comprehensive information display). clinical decision support includes rational drug use, antibiotic management, and cp, and focuses on medical quality procedure control. this procedure emphasizes the fundamental construction importance, and must provide technology and application support to stage ii development. fundamental design concept error or fundamental lack of technology will block the emr system development. phase ii will expand and optimize, and finally fulfill the target "hospital information construction with electronic medical records as the core", and achieve emr level 6 from the health department evaluation standard. emr implementing strategy the implementation strategy is: assured stable and safe medical order, making full use of the original fruit, detailed research, evaluation maturity of the original project, firstly reform the systems with poorer user experience, lower expandability, poorer maturity, and advance emr system gradually. xinhua hospital's new emr first abolishes paper based documentation, and applies controlled medical terminology classification system and structured technology, striving for computerized and understandable emr. second, it proposed innovative design concepts: implement "medical flow close-loop management" and "physician order close-loop management" by the emr system; proposed technology like "medical quality controlled integrated view". third, abandon the traditional hospital information management architecture. and then introduce a new concept taking emr as the core of hospital information management. it helps hospital management model with the core of human, finance, and material shifting to a management model with the core of healthcare quality. it follows the ministry of health "emr system functional application-oriented classification of evaluation methods and standards (trial)". and it provides experience for creating a new emr system in china.

title: host biology in light of the microbiome: ten principles of holobionts and hologenomes
display_name: Host Biology in Light of the Microbiome: Ten Principles of Holobionts and Hologenomes
abstract: groundbreaking research on the universality and diversity of microorganisms is now challenging the life sciences to upgrade fundamental theories that once seemed untouchable. to fully appreciate the change that the field is now undergoing, one has to place the epochs and foundational principles of darwin, mendel, and the modern synthesis in light of the current advances that are enabling a new vision for the central importance of microbiology. animals and plants are no longer heralded as autonomous entities but rather as biomolecular networks composed of the host plus its associated microbes, i.e., "holobionts." as such, their collective genomes forge a "hologenome," and models of animal and plant biology that do not account for these intergenomic associations are incomplete. here, we integrate these concepts into historical and contemporary visions of biology and summarize a predictive and refutable framework for their evaluation. specifically, we present ten principles that clarify and append what these concepts are and are not, explain how they both support and extend existing theory in the life sciences, and discuss their potential ramifications for the multifaceted approaches of zoology and botany. we anticipate that the conceptual and evidence-based foundation provided in this essay will serve as a roadmap for hypothesis-driven, experimentally validated research on holobionts and their hologenomes, thereby catalyzing the continued fusion of biology's subdisciplines. at a time when symbiotic microbes are recognized as fundamental to all aspects of animal and plant biology, the holobiont and hologenome concepts afford a holistic view of biological complexity that is consistent with the generally reductionist approaches of biology.

title: design and testing of an intramedullary nail implant enhanced with active feedback and wireless connectivity for precise limb lengthening
display_name: Design and Testing of an Intramedullary Nail Implant Enhanced with Active Feedback and Wireless Connectivity for Precise Limb Lengthening
abstract: this comprehensive study presents a pioneering approach to limb lengthening, leveraging the advancements in wireless technology to enhance orthopedic healthcare. historically, limb lengthening has been a response to discrepancies caused by fractures, diseases, or congenital defects, utilizing the body s innate ability to regenerate bone and surrounding tissues. traditionally, this involved external or internal fixation devices, such as the ilizarov and taylor spatial frames or the precice nail and fitbone. the focal point of this research is the development and testing of a wireless intramedullary nail implant prototype, controlled remotely via a mobile application. this implant comprises a microcontroller, bluetooth low energy module, a brushed dc motor controlled through an h-bridge, and a force sensor, all powered by medical-grade batteries. the integration of wireless technology facilitates patient autonomy in managing limb lengthening, reducing the need for frequent clinical visits. the methodology involves a detailed block diagram for our proposed work, outlining the process from treatment planning to the initiation of limb lengthening via the mobile application. osteogenesis, the formation of new bone tissue, plays a crucial role in this procedure, which includes pre-surgery assessment, osteotomy, latency, distraction, consolidation, and removal phases. key challenges addressed include custom battery design for efficient operation, size constraints, and overcoming signal interference due to the faraday cage effect. attenuation testing, simulating human tissue interaction, validates the implant s connectivity. in conclusion, this research marks a significant stride in orthopedic care, demonstrating the feasibility of a wireless implant for limb lengthening. it highlights the potential benefits of reduced clinical visits, cost efficiency, and patient convenience. despite limitations such as battery requirements and signal interference, this study opens avenues for future enhancements in patient-centered orthopedic treatments, signaling a transformative shift in managing limb length discrepancies.

institutions: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

abstract: somatic activating mutations in the phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase/akt/mtor pathway underlie heterogeneous segmental overgrowth phenotypes. because of the extreme differences among patients, we sought to characterize the phenotypic spectrum associated with different genotypes and mutation burdens, including a better understanding of associated complications and natural history. historically, the clinical diagnoses in patients with pik3ca activating mutations have included fibroadipose hyperplasia or overgrowth (fao), hemihyperplasia multiple lipomatosis (hhml), congenital lipomatous overgrowth, vascular malformations, epidermal nevi, scoliosis/skeletal and spinal (cloves) syndrome, macrodactyly, fibroadipose infiltrating lipomatosis, and the related megalencephaly syndromes, megalencephaly capillary malformation (mcap or m cm) and dysplastic megalencephaly (dmeg). a workshop was convened at the national institutes of health (nih) to discuss and develop a consensus document regarding diagnosis and treatment of patients with pik3ca associated somatic overgrowth disorders. participants in the workshop included a group of researchers from several institutions who have been studying these disorders and have published their findings, as well as representatives from patient advocacy and support groups. the umbrella term of pik3ca related overgrowth spectrum (pros) was agreed upon to encompass both the known and emerging clinical entities associated with somatic pik3ca mutations including, macrodactyly, fao, hhml, cloves, and related megalencephaly conditions. key clinical diagnostic features and criteria for testing were proposed, and testing approaches summarized. preliminary recommendations for a uniform approach to assessment of overgrowth and molecular diagnostic testing were determined. future areas to address include the surgical management of overgrowth tissue and vascular anomalies, the optimal approach to thrombosis risk, and the testing of potential pharmacologic therapies. 2014 the authors. american journal of medical genetics part a published by wiley periodicals, inc.

abstract: abstract we present here the first update of the 2013 efsumb (european federation of societies for ultrasound in medicine and biology) guidelines and recommendations on the clinical use of elastography, focused on the assessment of diffuse liver disease. the first part (long version) of these guidelines and recommendations deals with the basic principles of elastography and provides an update of how the technology has changed. the practical advantages and disadvantages associated with each of the techniques are described, and guidance is provided regarding optimization of scanning technique, image display, image interpretation, reporting of data and some of the known image artefacts. the second part provides clinical information about the practical use of elastography equipment and the interpretation of results in the assessment of diffuse liver disease and analyzes the main findings based on published studies, stressing the evidence from meta-analyses. the role of elastography in different etiologies of liver disease and in several clinical scenarios is also discussed. all of the recommendations are judged with regard to their evidence-based strength according to the oxford centre for evidence-based medicine levels of evidence. this updated document is intended to act as a reference and to provide a practical guide for both beginners and advanced clinical users.

title: evidence based guidelines support integrated disease management as the optimal model of haemophilia care
display_name: Evidence‐based guidelines support integrated disease management as the optimal model of haemophilia care
abstract: the series of papers in this supplement of haemophilia provide important evidence supporting the use of an integrated disease management model to deliver care to persons with haemophilia. the lead manuscript by pai and co-authors reports the national hemophilia foundation (nhf)-mcmaster guideline on care models for haemophilia management 1. using direct evidence from published literature and the haemophilia community, as well as indirect evidence from other chronic diseases, the guideline panel has created evidence-based recommendations. the guideline methodology utilized the suggested principles for developing transparent, evidence-based guidelines promoted by the institute of medicine, the national guideline clearinghouse, and the grading of recommendations, assessment, development, and evaluation (grade) working group. the conclusion that this systemic evidence review supports is that the integrated care model, as is utilized within the us federally funded network of hemophilia treatment centers (htcs), should be advocated for optimal care of persons with haemophilia. these guidelines will provide a catalyst to promote harmonization of care delivery and reduce practice variations within the us htc network. this guideline will inform the htc network how best to prioritize additional high-value research to fill data gaps or strengthen the evidence base as outlined in the manuscript. the network is now prepared to support agreed upon evidence-based performance benchmarks that would allow for both internal and external evaluation of adherence to best practices and to benchmark available services within an htc, potentially leading to the establishment of a us htc self-audit or accreditation system as has been developed in other countries. these guidelines will provide the ideal starting point for defining the best practices in an evidence-based manner and build a foundation for the development of key metrics that can be tracked within the network, supporting research studies, advocacy at state and federal levels, and highlighting the benefits of the implementation of those best practices by the htc integrated care models 2. to provide a historical perspective, nhf established the medical and scientific advisory council (masac) in 1954 to bring together physician experts in the field of coagulation to advance care for patients with haemophilia and develop recommendations for their treatment. the vision was to connect physicians and researchers to discuss challenges in care and research for this rare but severe bleeding disorder. masac has served a crucial role in disseminating information, serving as an intermediary between scientific and medical organizations and patients, the end-users of blood products. recommendations from masac have detailed advances in therapy and communicated how to use them effectively, fostering communication to the broader clinical community and accelerating progress for patients. its membership now includes not only physicians, scientists and patients from the bleeding disorder community but also representatives from the food and drug administration (fda), centers for disease control and prevention (cdc), national institutes of health (nih), the health resources and services administration/maternal and child health bureau (hrsa/mchb), world federation of hemophilia (wfh) and the american thrombosis and hemostasis network (athn). in 2012, at the urging of the nhf masac chair, nhf held a strategic summit to develop a plan for haemophilia care within the changing us healthcare landscape largely due to the changes occurring following the enactment of the affordable care act, the major health care reform legislation 3. the major tenets of the healthcare reform include: health insurance coverage not tied to employment, portability of that coverage with minimal exclusions, affordability, choice, quality, prevention and sustainability all of these being highly relevant for how haemophilia care is provided within the us. to address the challenges of the shifting healthcare landscape, the summit identified the need to strengthen the evidence base for haemophilia care and promotion of the integrated care model. it was determined that generating and maintaining evidence-based guidelines would require a complete comprehensive assessment of existing guidelines and resolutions, identifying gaps and prioritizing the standards that would need updating, and implementing a systematic process for updating and dissemination. following a scoping process by a working group of the current and former masac leaders and others, nine priority guideline topics were identified. the phase 1 priority as determined by the findings of the summit and the scoping working group would focus on models of haemophilia care with future guidelines following the framework established by this first guideline with a focus on more specific aspects of care and patient populations. this guideline is a foundational one upon which more specific guidelines addressing other aspects of care may be developed and will inform future areas of needed research. the focus on models of haemophilia care is timely. since 1974, congress authorized and has funded haemophilia programmes within the hrsa/mchb, and in the 1980s and 1990s, cdc surveillance and blood safety programmes were established. these programmes recognized that individuals with bleeding disorders had difficulty obtaining quality care due to the rarity and complexity of their disease. this funding led to the development of centres of excellence, designated as haemophilia treatment centres, which focused on the provision of individualized treatment plans, preventative care and education. they espoused the common goal of maximizing coordination, effectiveness and efficiency in care delivery. the core htc team has traditionally included a haematologist, specialized haemophilia nurse, physical therapist and social worker. this guideline also identifies access to a specialized coagulation laboratory to be a critical element to support the integrated care team. however, beyond this core group, other care providers (e.g. dental professionals, genetic counsellors, orthopedists, infectious disease specialists, etc.) are either available on-site or via established partnerships. additional clinical practice guidelines would accomplish many important goals: the effectiveness of the htc model has been well documented through studies conducted by both hrsa/mchb and the cdc. from a 1985 analysis, hrsa/mchb reported the outcome data from 31 centres through the first 10 years of the htc network, demonstrating that the network increased the number of patients with haemophilia regularly receiving comprehensive care by 326%, while the number of patients with the ability to treat at home increased by 390% with a 73% reduction in missed school/work days during the same period 4. subsequently, the hemophilia surveillance study was reported by the cdc in 1995, utilizing data sources from the htcs, the cdc and state health departments in six states that identified all patients within these states with haemophilia, including those treated outside of an htc 5. the study documented a 40% decrease in mortality among patients treated at htcs, which was particularly notable given that htcs provided care to a higher proportion of severely affected patients and patients with complications including inhibitors, liver disease and hiv/aids as compared to haemophilia patients managed in non-htc settings. among the 2950 patients followed over 3 years, the relative mortality rate increased by 70% and the relative hospitalization rate increased by 40% for patients who received care outside of the htc network. despite the impressive outcome results, these studies are now 20 30 years old, and there exists wide variation in the characteristics and capabilities of current htcs in terms of funding, geography covered, affiliation (e.g. hospital/university, standalone, etc.), available provider specialties and patient populations served. within the shifting us healthcare landscape, all stakeholders are looking for evidence that the integrated care models that are in place within the htcs are responding to the major tenets of healthcare reform and continuing to deliver with respect to the quality of care for haemophilia and other bleeding disorders. this guideline confirms and updates this prior research. however, the guideline takes note of the paucity of data addressing some important patient outcomes and highlights the importance of unified data systems in us htcs to facilitate research. the reality of the current healthcare environment requires the presence of a process to evaluate the successes and shortcomings of various models of care delivery and their impact on patient important outcomes. the htc infrastructure provides a unique model to track, in a longitudinal manner, the safety of new emerging therapies, as well as contribute valuable evidence to the development of cost-effective treatment paradigms that could serve as a role model for other chronic disease. htcs must build further capacity to collect and analyse data as well, to power higher quality, comprehensive studies. we commend the work of the nhf and investigators at mcmaster university in developing this important guideline and extend our thanks to the guideline panel members for their efforts over the past 2 years. we believe the guideline is an important addition to the evidence base of haemophilia care and management. masac and nhf are prepared to continue our efforts to improve the evidence base. we are pleased to report that the nhf-mcmaster guideline on care models for haemophilia management have been endorsed by the american society of hematology (may 27, 2016), the international society for thrombosis and haemostasis (may 28, 2016), and the world federation of hemophilia (may 20, 2016). we encourage others to collaborate and take advantage of this unique new resource for our community. swp is the current chair of the nhf medical and scientific advisory council (masac). cmk served as masac chair from 2008 to 2015. the authors stated that they had no interests which might be perceived as posing a conflict or bias.

title: a guide to conducting a standalone systematic literature review
display_name: A Guide to Conducting a Standalone Systematic Literature Review
abstract: many scholars are not well trained in conducting a standalone literature review, a scholarly paper that in its entirety summarizes and synthesizes knowledge from a prior body of research. numerous guides that exist for information systems (is) research mainly concentrate on only certain parts of the process; few span the entire process. this paper introduces the rigorous, standardized methodology for the systematic literature review (also called systematic review) to is scholars. this comprehensive guide extends the base methodology from the health sciences and other fields with numerous adaptations to meet the needs of methodologically diverse fields such as is research, especially those that involve including and synthesizing both quantitative and qualitative studies. moreover, this guide provides many examples from is research and provides references to guides with further helpful details for conducting a rigorous and valuable literature review. although tailored to is research, it is sufficiently broad to be applicable and valuable to scholars from any social science field.
